definition.s_pred: per-(object,k) Spearman(anchor pred ranking, het pred ranking); median over cells
definition.s_real: per-(object,k) Spearman(anchor realized ang ranking, het realized ang ranking); median over cells
definition.fit_arm: per-(object,k) Spearman(pred, realized) within arm; median over cells
definition.cell_note: n=4 informed units per cell; degenerate (all-tie) cells skipped

reading: failure is truth-end decoupling, NOT sigma misspecification
reading_rule: decoupled: s_pred >= 0.9 AND s_real <= 0.0; symmetric: |fit_het - cross_ah| <= 0.15 AND |fit_anc - cross_ha| <= 0.15; both -> the failure is truth-end (heterogeneity re-orders the realized benefits while the predicted orderings barely move), NOT sigma misspecification (a misspecified-sigma predictor would have moved: its ranking is the thing that would be wrong)
conclusion_text: The het-arm 0.353 below-chance result is NOT a sigma-model misspecification artifact: handing the predictor the TRUE per-light sigma changes its policy ordering by only 0.051 in rank correlation (S_pred = 0.948683), and the matched predictor (fit_het -0.777778) performs the same as the anchor's uniform one on het truth (cross_ah -0.737865). The criterion's policy ordering is insensitive to heterogeneity while the realized-benefit ordering is highly sensitive to it (S_real = -0.324781) -- the two decouple, and the per-light J_A ordering loses its decision validity under per-light heterogeneity regardless of sigma specification.
